newsitem.title: USA: "Rafters" relax on Miami Beach after fleeing Cuba.
newsitem.headline: "Rafters" relax on Miami Beach after fleeing Cuba.

text.p: Eight Cubans relaxed in deck chairs and enjoyed snacks brought by Florida residents when they landed in Miami Beach on Monday after more than two days at sea in a wooden boat from Cuba, police said.

A security guard from a seafront condomium spotted the five men and three women when they came ashore in Miami's most fashionable district in the morning. "He told them to wait for us to arrive. We found them sitting on beach chairs," police detective Alfred Boza told Reuters.

People on the beach and nearby residents brought them coffee, water, food, blankets and clothes. "They looked in pretty good shape," Bozas said, adding: "It's been some time since we've had an arrival like this."
The refugees, who included a married couple, were aged between 18 and 40. They said they had left the Cuban town of Sagua La Grande early on Saturday.
They were handed over to the Border Patrol pending a decision on whether they would be granted asylum.
